deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is an archival cover or wrapper sheet for bundle Math. 34. It was most likely written by a later cataloguer of the Gauss Nachlass, not by Gauss himself, judging from the Kurrent-style German labelling, the 'G. B. Nr.' references and the archival 'Ga'/'Га' markers.

It records the following:
- The bundle contains 'Ein Zettel aus G. B. Nr. [blank]'. 'Ein' (one) replaces a struck-through '2'. G. B. means Gauss-Bibliothek, Gauss's personal library, now in Göttingen; the shelf number was left blank.
- The slip was found inside Gauss's copy of Lobachevsky's Russian paper 'Применение воображаемой геометрии к некоторым интегралам' ('Application of imaginary geometry to certain integrals', Kazan, Uchenye Zapiski 1836).
- A second entry is struck through: 'und aus G. B. Nr. Lobatschewsky, Geometrische Untersuchungen zur Theorie der Parallellinien' (Berlin 1840). The cataloguer apparently first thought there were two slips, one from each Lobachevsky volume, and then corrected this to a single slip.
- 'Га' is the Cyrillic counterpart of the shelf mark 'Ga'. 'Math' is the classification.

Context from the next page (the slip itself, headed 'Astralgéometrie'):
- Gauss computes the volume of an infinitely thin prism ABCabc in non-Euclidean ('astral') space. The edges Aa, Bb, Cc are normal to the plane ABC, Aa is the minimal (infinitesimal) distance between the two planes, and AB is normal to BC.
- The formula is Volume = 1/2 · Aa · BC · sin(i·AD)/i. Since sin(ix)/i = sinh(x), this equals 1/2 · Aa · BC · sinh(AD), in units where the curvature constant is 1.
- Thus the volume element involves a hyperbolic sine in place of a Euclidean length. This is exactly the kind of volume computation Lobachevsky's 1836 paper uses to evaluate definite integrals.
- That the slip sat inside this specific paper fits Gauss's known reading of Lobachevsky in Russian in the 1840s.

No derivation on this page needs reconstruction.

results.what: Archival provenance note: a Gauss slip on 'Astralgeometrie' was kept inside Gauss's copy of Lobachevsky's 1836 'Application of imaginary geometry to certain integrals'; a second attribution to the 1840 'Geometrische Untersuchungen' was cancelled.
(Context, next page) Volume of an infinitesimal right prism in hyperbolic space expressed via sin(i x)/i = sinh x.
results.modern_name: Hyperbolic volume element / Lobachevsky's use of non-Euclidean volumes to evaluate integrals

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a cataloguer's wrapper with no mathematics. Gauss's ownership and study of Lobachevsky's works, including the Russian papers, is well documented in his letters to Schumacher and Gerling and in the Gauss-Bibliothek holdings.

checkable.asserts: sin(i x)/i = sinh(x), the identity behind the next page's prism-volume formula 1/2*Aa*BC*sin(i*AD)/i.

transcription_corrections: The title word is written in old orthography with a final i: 'Примѣненiе' rather than 'Примѣнение'.
In 'воображаемой' the 'а' is a later insertion marked with a bracket; the original writing was 'воображемой'. The transcription's {+а+} is correct.
'Ein' is written above a heavily struck-through '2' before 'Zettel', i.e. 'Ein Zettel' (originally '2 Zettel'). This matches the cancellation of the second 'und aus G. B. Nr.' line.
The bracketed name above the Russian title is the transliteration '(Lobatschewskij)', written in German script.
